modules.title: A. Band theory
modules.doc:
This module provides a home for the theory of Bloch Hamiltonians and states, band projectors,
energy bands and gaps, and band geometry. Generic quantum-mechanical infrastructure should be
reused from Physlib rather than redefined here.

modules.title: A. Condensed matter
modules.doc:
Condensed matter physics studies the collective behavior of matter, from crystalline structure
and lattice models to interacting phases, topology, and material response.

## A.1. Scope

- `Crystal` covers crystal structures, reciprocal-space descriptions, symmetries, and dynamics.
- `LatticeModels` covers Hamiltonian models whose degrees of freedom live on lattices.
- `BandTheory` covers Bloch descriptions, energy bands, gaps, and band geometry.
- `ManyBody` covers correlations, quasiparticles, Green functions, and interacting matter.
- `Topology` covers topological phases and invariants in condensed matter systems.
- `Response` covers transport and the linear, optical, and nonlinear response of materials.

## A.2. Existing modules

Existing condensed-matter modules currently include `TightBindingChain` and `Thermoelectric`.
They remain in their existing locations and have not been reorganized into the scopes above.

modules.title: Crystals, cells and sites
modules.doc:
A crystal is a finite unit cell repeated periodically.

## i. Overview

The goal is to construct crystals such as the square, hexagonal, fcc, bcc and hcp lattices. The
standard starting point is a unit cell repeated by translations; see the reference below. We
start combinatorially, with a unit cell that repeats many times over. This periodicity is modeled
by a finitely generated abelian group `G`, written additively, with `ℤᵈ` as the prototypical
example. Each unit cell consists of finitely many things, such as atoms, spins or orbitals, which
are labeled by a type `F`. Repeating the cell gives one site `⟨n, i⟩` for every cell `n : G` and
label `i : F`. Translation acts only on the cell:

`a +ᵥ ⟨n, i⟩ = ⟨a + n, i⟩`.

A crystal with one site per cell has a single label, while the honeycomb and hcp lattices have two.
A species assignment gives each label a species, for example a chemical element.

For `ℤᵈ` the sites form an infinite array, and for `(ℤ/mℤ)ᵈ` a finite array with periodic
boundary conditions. Coordinates in space, and with them distances and angles, are not part of this
description and is added in other files.

## ii. Key results

- `Crystal` : a finitely generated abelian translation group with a finite, nonempty unit cell.
- `Crystal.ofUnitCell` : the crystal obtained by repeating a labeled unit cell.
- `Crystal.Site` : a site given by its cell and unit-cell label.
- `Crystal.Site.ref` : the site with a given label in the reference cell.
- `Crystal.Species` : a species assignment, one species for each unit-cell label.
- `Crystal.Site.mem_orbit_iff_label_eq` : the translates of a site are exactly the sites with the
  same label.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The unit cell
- B. Constructing a crystal from a unit cell
- C. Sites and their finiteness
- D. Translation symmetry
- E. Species

## iv. References

* F. Göhmann, *Introduction to Solid State Physics*, lecture L3, Section 3.1, for the standard
  description of a crystal as translated copies of a unit cell. [ref: goehmann_solid_state_2021]

sections.text: ## A. The unit cell
## B. Constructing a crystal from a unit cell
## C. Sites and their finiteness
## D. Translation symmetry
## E. Species

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal
declarations.doc:
A crystal with finitely generated abelian translation group `G` and a finite, nonempty unit
cell. The sites are one copy of each unit-cell label in every translated cell.
declarations.statement:
structure Crystal (G : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [AddGroup.FG G] where
  /-- The labels of the things in one unit cell, such as atoms, spins or orbitals. -/
  UnitCell : Type*
  /-- The unit cell has finitely many labels. -/
  [finiteUnitCell : Finite UnitCell]
  /-- The unit cell has at least one label. -/
  [nonemptyUnitCell : Nonempty UnitCell]

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.ofUnitCell
declarations.doc:
Construct a crystal by repeating a unit cell with labels `F`.
The group `G` indexes translated cells; `⟨n, i⟩` is the site with label `i` in cell `n`.
declarations.statement:
abbrev ofUnitCell (G : Type*) (F : Type*) [AddCommGroup G] [AddGroup.FG G]
    [Finite F] [Nonempty F] : Crystal G

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site
declarations.doc: A site of `C`, with label `i` in cell `n`.
declarations.statement:
structure Site (C : Crystal G) where
  /-- The cell containing this site. -/
  cell : G
  /-- The label of this site within its cell. -/
  label : C.UnitCell

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.ref
declarations.doc: The site with label `i` in the reference cell, the cell `0`.
declarations.statement: abbrev Site.ref {C : Crystal G} (i : C.UnitCell) : C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.cell_ref
declarations.doc: The reference site lies in the cell `0`.
declarations.statement: lemma Site.cell_ref {C : Crystal G} (i : C.UnitCell) : (Site.ref i).cell = 0

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.label_ref
declarations.doc: The reference site has the label `i`.
declarations.statement: lemma Site.label_ref {C : Crystal G} (i : C.UnitCell) : (Site.ref i).label = i

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.siteEquiv
declarations.doc: A site is a pair of its unit-cell label and its cell.
declarations.statement: def siteEquiv (C : Crystal G) : C.Site ≃ C.UnitCell × G

declarations.doc: Sites can be compared when cells and unit-cell labels can be compared.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] : DecidableEq C.Site

declarations.doc: A finite set of cells and a finite unit cell give a finite set of sites.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) [Fintype G] [Fintype C.UnitCell] : Fintype C.Site

declarations.doc: A finite translation group, as for periodic boundary conditions, gives a finite crystal.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) [Finite G] : Finite C.Site

declarations.doc: Every crystal has a site in its reference cell.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) : Nonempty C.Site

declarations.doc: Translate a site to another cell, preserving its unit-cell label.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) : AddAction G C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.vadd_def
declarations.doc: Translation changes a site's cell and preserves its label.
declarations.statement:
lemma Site.vadd_def {C : Crystal G} (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    a +ᵥ x = ⟨a + x.cell, x.label⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.cell_vadd
declarations.doc: The cell of a translated site is the translated cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma Site.cell_vadd {C : Crystal G} (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    (a +ᵥ x).cell = a + x.cell

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.label_vadd
declarations.doc: Translation preserves the label of a site.
declarations.statement:
lemma Site.label_vadd {C : Crystal G} (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    (a +ᵥ x).label = x.label

declarations.doc:
Translation acts freely: translations are injective on sites, and different translations move
a site to different sites.
declarations.statement: instance (C : Crystal G) : IsCancelVAdd G C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Site.mem_orbit_iff_label_eq
declarations.doc: The translates of a site are exactly the sites with the same label.
declarations.statement:
lemma Site.mem_orbit_iff_label_eq {C : Crystal G} (x y : C.Site) :
    y ∈ AddAction.orbit G x ↔ x.label = y.label

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Species
declarations.doc:
A species assignment gives each label of the unit cell a species in `Q`, for example a chemical
element. The same assignment holds in every cell.
declarations.statement: abbrev Species (C : Crystal G) (Q : Type*)

modules.title: Bonds in a crystal
modules.doc:
A bond connects sites in two unit cells of a crystal.

## i. Overview

A bond `⟨i, j, d⟩` joins the site with label `i` in cell `n` to the site with label `j`
in cell `n + d`. Translating both endpoints gives another copy of the same bond.

## ii. Key results

- `Bond` : a source label, a target label and the displacement between their cells.
- `Bond.Links` : the relation between sites connected by a bond.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Bonds in a unit cell

## iv. References

* F. Göhmann, *Introduction to Solid State Physics*, lecture L3, Section 3.1, for the standard
  description of a crystal. [ref: goehmann_solid_state_2021]

sections.text: ## A. Bonds in a unit cell

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond
declarations.doc: A bond from `source` in one cell to `target` in the cell displaced by `displacement`.
declarations.statement:
structure Bond (C : Crystal G) where
  /-- The site label at the start of the bond. -/
  source : C.UnitCell
  /-- The site label at the end of the bond. -/
  target : C.UnitCell
  /-- Translation from the source cell to the target cell. -/
  displacement : G

declarations.doc: Bonds can be compared when cells and unit-cell labels can be compared.
declarations.statement: instance {C : Crystal G} [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] : DecidableEq (Bond C)

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.Links
declarations.doc: Site `x` is the source and site `y` is the target of this bond.
declarations.statement: def Links (b : Bond C) (x y : C.Site) : Prop

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.links_reference
declarations.doc: Every bond links the reference site of its source to the site its displacement points to.
declarations.statement: lemma links_reference (b : Bond C) : b.Links (Site.ref b.source) ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.eq_of_links
declarations.doc: Two bonds linking the same pair of sites are equal.
declarations.statement:
lemma eq_of_links {b b' : Bond C} {x y : C.Site} (h : b.Links x y) (h' : b'.Links x y) :
    b = b'

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Bond.links_vadd
declarations.doc: Translating the endpoints gives another copy of the same bond.
declarations.statement:
lemma links_vadd (b : Bond C) (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    b.Links (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ b.Links x y

declarations.doc: The source and target of a bond can be checked from their site addresses.
declarations.statement: instance [DecidableEq G] [DecidableEq C.UnitCell] (b : Bond C) : DecidableRel b.Links

modules.title: Bravais lattices
modules.doc:
A Bravais lattice with one site per cell, repeated by `d` independent translations, and its
embedding given by `d` primitive vectors.

## i. Overview

A Bravais lattice of dimension `d` is the crystal with translation group `ℤᵈ` and a unit cell with
a single site. Its embedding in a normed space `E` is fixed by the `d` primitive vectors, one for
each generator of `ℤᵈ`: the cell `n` goes to the integer combination of these vectors with
coefficients `n j`, and the single site sits at the origin of its cell. The different lattice types
differ only in these vectors, so the general facts are proved here once.

## ii. Key results

- `Crystal.bravais` : the crystal with translation group `ℤᵈ` and one site per cell.
- `Crystal.Embedding.ofVectors` : the embedding of `Crystal.bravais d` given by `d` primitive
  vectors.
- `Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors` : the position of a site is the integer combination of
  the primitive vectors given by its cell.
- `Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_ofVectors_iff` : the embedding is space filling exactly when the
  primitive vectors span the space.
- `Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors_injective` : linearly independent primitive vectors give
  distinct positions to distinct sites.
- `Crystal.Embedding.finrank_eq_of_ofVectors` : a space-filling embedding with linearly
  independent primitive vectors lives in a space of dimension `d`.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The crystal
- B. The embedding
- C. Spanning and independence

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. The crystal
## B. The embedding
## C. Spanning and independence

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.bravais
declarations.doc:
The Bravais lattice of dimension `d`: the translation group is `ℤᵈ` and the unit cell has a
single site.
declarations.statement: def bravais (d : ℕ) : Crystal (Fin d → ℤ)

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.ofVectors
declarations.doc: The embedding of the Bravais lattice of dimension `d` given by `d` primitive vectors.
declarations.statement: def ofVectors (v : Fin d → E) : Embedding (bravais d) E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors
declarations.doc:
The position of a site is the integer combination of the primitive vectors given by its
cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_ofVectors (v : Fin d → E) (x : (bravais d).Site) :
    (ofVectors v).position x = ∑ j, x.cell j • v j

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_ofVectors_iff
declarations.doc:
The embedding of a Bravais lattice is space filling exactly when the primitive vectors span
the space.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSpaceFilling_ofVectors_iff (v : Fin d → E) :
    (ofVectors v).IsSpaceFilling ↔ Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range v) = ⊤

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_ofVectors_injective
declarations.doc: Linearly independent primitive vectors give distinct positions to distinct sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma position_ofVectors_injective {v : Fin d → E} (hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v) :
    Function.Injective (ofVectors v).position

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.finrank_eq_of_ofVectors
declarations.doc:
A space-filling embedding of a Bravais lattice with linearly independent primitive vectors
lives in a space of dimension `d`.
declarations.statement:
lemma finrank_eq_of_ofVectors {v : Fin d → E} (hv : LinearIndependent ℝ v)
    (h : (ofVectors v).IsSpaceFilling) : Module.finrank ℝ E = d

modules.title: A crystal in space
modules.doc:
Embedding of a crystal into a space.

## i. Overview

Given a normed additive commutative group `E`, an embedding sends each translation of the crystal to
a vector in `E` and each site of the reference cell to a point in `E`. The site `(n, i)` is then
placed at the vector of `n` plus the point of `i`. The embedding is space filling if the vectors of
the translations span `E`.

## ii. Key results

- `Crystal.Embedding` : the vectors `ρ` of the translations and the positions `p` of the
  sites of the reference cell, in a normed group.
- `Crystal.Embedding.positionHom` : the positions commute with the translations, as an equivariant
  map of the sites.
- `Crystal.Embedding.position_vadd` : translating a site translates its position.
- `Crystal.Embedding.dist_position_vadd` : translating two sites does not change the
  distance between their positions.
- `Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling` : the vectors of the translations span the space.
- `Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_iff` : space filling can be checked on a generating set.
- `Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finiteDimensional` : a space-filling embedding lies in a
  finite-dimensional space.
- `Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finrank_eq_rank` : the dimension of the space equals the rank
  of the translation group when the vectors of a basis of the group are linearly independent.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Vectors and positions
- B. Filling the space

## iv. References

* None.

sections.text: ## A. Vectors and positions
## B. Filling the space

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding
declarations.doc:
An embedding of a crystal in a normed group `E`. It assigns a vector to each translation and a
position to each site of the reference cell.
declarations.statement:
structure Embedding (C : Crystal G) (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] where
  /-- The vector of a translation. -/
  vector : G →+ E
  /-- The position of the site with a given label in the reference cell. -/
  basis : C.UnitCell → E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position
declarations.doc: The site `(n, i)` sits at the vector of `n` plus the position of the label `i`.
declarations.statement: def position (x : C.Site) : E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.position_vadd
declarations.doc: Translating a site by `a` translates its position by the vector of `a`.
declarations.statement: lemma position_vadd (a : G) (x : C.Site) : R.position (a +ᵥ x) = R.vector a + R.position x

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.action
declarations.doc: The translation group acts on the space by its vectors.
declarations.statement: abbrev action : AddAction G E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.positionHom
declarations.doc: The positions commute with the translations.
declarations.statement: def positionHom : letI := R.action; AddActionHom (id : G → G) C.Site E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.dist_position_vadd
declarations.doc: Translating two sites does not change the distance between their positions.
declarations.statement:
lemma dist_position_vadd (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    Dist.dist (R.position (a +ᵥ x)) (R.position (a +ᵥ y)) =
      Dist.dist (R.position x) (R.position y)

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling
declarations.doc:
The embedding is space filling if the vectors of the translations span the space, so that the
crystal repeats in every direction.
declarations.statement: def IsSpaceFilling : Prop

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.isSpaceFilling_iff
declarations.doc:
An embedding fills the space exactly when the vectors of a generating set of the translation
group span it.
declarations.statement:
lemma isSpaceFilling_iff {S : Set G} (hS : AddSubgroup.closure S = ⊤) :
    R.IsSpaceFilling ↔ Submodule.span ℝ (R.vector '' S) = ⊤

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finiteDimensional
declarations.doc: A space-filling embedding is in a finite-dimensional space.
declarations.statement: lemma IsSpaceFilling.finiteDimensional (h : R.IsSpaceFilling) : FiniteDimensional ℝ E

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.Embedding.IsSpaceFilling.finrank_eq_rank
declarations.doc:
The dimension equals the rank of the translation group when the vectors of a basis of the
group are linearly independent over `ℝ`.
declarations.statement:
lemma IsSpaceFilling.finrank_eq_rank (h : R.IsSpaceFilling) {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    (B : Module.Basis ι ℤ G) (hB : LinearIndependent ℝ (R.vector ∘ B)) :
    Module.finrank ℝ E = Module.finrank ℤ G

modules.title: Periodic graphs of crystals
modules.doc:
A finite set of bonds, repeated in every unit cell, gives the connections of a crystal.

## i. Overview

A crystal is a set of sites with a translation action. Connections between sites, such as the
nearest-neighbor links of a square lattice, give it a graph. Since the crystal is periodic, so is
its graph: translating both ends of a connection preserves adjacency,

`Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ Adj x y`.

It is enough to list the connections once. A finite set of bonds gives a periodic graph, and
conversely every periodic graph in which each site has finitely many neighbors comes from finitely
many bonds.

## ii. Key results

- `PeriodicGraph` : a graph on the sites that is invariant under translation and has finitely
  many neighbors at each site.
- `PeriodicGraph.ofBonds` : the periodic graph generated by a finite set of bonds.
- `PeriodicGraph.eq_ofBonds` : every periodic graph is generated by finitely many bonds.
- `PeriodicGraph.degree_vadd` : every copy of a site has the same number of neighbors.
- `PeriodicGraph.graphAutomorphisms` : the adjacency-preserving permutations of the sites.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. Translation-invariant connectivity
- B. Building the graph from bonds
- C. Adjacency depends on cell differences
- D. The periodic graph of a finite set of bonds
- E. Every periodic graph comes from bonds
- F. Graph automorphisms

## iv. References

* F. Göhmann, *Introduction to Solid State Physics*, lecture L3, Section 3.1, for the standard
  description of a crystal. [ref: goehmann_solid_state_2021]

sections.text: ## A. Translation-invariant connectivity
## B. Building the graph from bonds
## C. Adjacency depends on cell differences
## D. The periodic graph of a finite set of bonds
## E. Every periodic graph comes from bonds
## F. Graph automorphisms

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph
declarations.doc:
A periodic pattern of undirected connections between crystal sites, with finitely many
neighbors at each site.
declarations.statement:
structure PeriodicGraph (C : Crystal G) where
  /-- The undirected connections between crystal sites. -/
  toSimpleGraph : SimpleGraph C.Site
  /-- Translating both sites preserves their connection. -/
  adj_vadd : ∀ (a : G) (x y : C.Site),
    toSimpleGraph.Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ toSimpleGraph.Adj x y
  /-- Each site is connected to only finitely many other sites. -/
  [locallyFinite : toSimpleGraph.LocallyFinite]

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ext
declarations.doc: Periodic graphs are equal when their underlying graphs are.
declarations.statement: lemma ext {g g' : PeriodicGraph C} (h : g.toSimpleGraph = g'.toSimpleGraph) : g = g'

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.translateIso
declarations.doc: A translation is an automorphism of the graph.
declarations.statement: def translateIso (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) : g.toSimpleGraph ≃g g.toSimpleGraph

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.degree_vadd
declarations.doc: The degree, the number of neighbors, is the same for all translates of a site.
declarations.statement:
lemma degree_vadd (g : PeriodicGraph C) (a : G) (x : C.Site) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.degree (a +ᵥ x) = g.toSimpleGraph.degree x

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.degree_cell
declarations.doc: The degree of a site depends only on its label.
declarations.statement:
lemma degree_cell (g : PeriodicGraph C) (n : G) (i : C.UnitCell) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.degree ⟨n, i⟩ = g.toSimpleGraph.degree (Site.ref i)

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.graphOfBonds
declarations.doc: The undirected graph generated by translating every bond in the set.
declarations.statement: def graphOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : SimpleGraph C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_graphOfBonds
declarations.doc: Two sites are adjacent when they are different and joined by a bond in either direction.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_graphOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x y : C.Site) :
    (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧ ∃ b ∈ bonds, b.Links x y ∨ b.Links y x

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.graphOfBonds_adj_vadd
declarations.doc: Adjacency generated by bonds is unchanged by a common cell translation.
declarations.statement:
lemma graphOfBonds_adj_vadd (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (a : G) (x y : C.Site) :
    (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj (a +ᵥ x) (a +ᵥ y) ↔ (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj x y

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_iff
declarations.doc: Adjacency depends only on the labels of the sites and the difference of their cells.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_iff (g : PeriodicGraph C) (x y : C.Site) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y ↔
      g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (Site.ref x.label) ⟨y.cell - x.cell, y.label⟩

declarations.doc: Connections generated by a finite set of bonds can be decided.
declarations.statement: instance (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : DecidableRel (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.candidates
declarations.doc: The sites reached from `x` by following a bond forwards or backwards.
declarations.statement: def candidates (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x : C.Site) : Finset C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.neighborsOfBonds
declarations.doc: The neighbors of a site in the graph generated by finitely many bonds.
declarations.statement: def neighborsOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x : C.Site) : Finset C.Site

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_neighborsOfBonds
declarations.doc: The enumerated neighbors are exactly the adjacent sites.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_neighborsOfBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x y : C.Site) :
    y ∈ neighborsOfBonds bonds x ↔ (graphOfBonds bonds).Adj x y

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.ofBonds
declarations.doc: The periodic graph obtained by repeating the given bonds in every cell.
declarations.statement: def ofBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) : PeriodicGraph C

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_ofBonds
declarations.doc: Two sites are adjacent in the graph from bonds when they are joined by one of the bonds.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_ofBonds (bonds : Finset (Bond C)) (x y : C.Site) :
    (ofBonds bonds).toSimpleGraph.Adj x y ↔ x ≠ y ∧ ∃ b ∈ bonds, b.Links x y ∨ b.Links y x

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.bonds
declarations.doc: The bonds that join a site of the reference cell to one of its neighbors.
declarations.statement: def bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Finset (Bond C)

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.mem_bonds
declarations.doc: A bond of `g.bonds` joins a site of the reference cell to one of its neighbors.
declarations.statement:
lemma mem_bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) (b : Bond C) :
    b ∈ g.bonds ↔ g.toSimpleGraph.Adj (Site.ref b.source) ⟨b.displacement, b.target⟩

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_of_links
declarations.doc: Sites joined by a bond of `g.bonds` are adjacent in `g`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_of_links (g : PeriodicGraph C) {b : Bond C} (hb : b ∈ g.bonds) {x y : C.Site}
    (h : b.Links x y) : g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.adj_iff_mem_bonds
declarations.doc: Sites joined by a bond are adjacent exactly when the bond is one of `g.bonds`.
declarations.statement:
lemma adj_iff_mem_bonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) {b : Bond C} {x y : C.Site} (h : b.Links x y) :
    g.toSimpleGraph.Adj x y ↔ b ∈ g.bonds

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.toSimpleGraph_eq_graphOfBonds
declarations.doc: Every periodic graph is generated by the finitely many bonds leaving the reference cell.
declarations.statement:
lemma toSimpleGraph_eq_graphOfBonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) :
    g.toSimpleGraph = graphOfBonds g.bonds

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.eq_ofBonds
declarations.doc:
Every periodic graph is generated by the finitely many bonds leaving the reference
cell.
declarations.statement: lemma eq_ofBonds (g : PeriodicGraph C) : g = ofBonds g.bonds

declarations.name: Physlib.CondensedMatter.Crystal.PeriodicGraph.graphAutomorphisms
declarations.doc: The automorphism group of the underlying graph, without requiring crystal symmetry.
declarations.statement: def graphAutomorphisms (g : PeriodicGraph C) : Subgroup (Equiv.Perm C.Site)

modules.title: A. Lattice models
modules.doc:
This module provides a home for hopping Hamiltonians, tight-binding and Hubbard-type models,
and spin lattice models. A future design issue is the relation between real-space lattice
Hamiltonians and momentum-space Bloch Hamiltonians.

modules.title: A. Many-body physics
modules.doc:
This module provides a home for correlation functions, quasiparticles, Green functions,
mean-field descriptions, and interacting quantum matter.

modules.title: A. Response
modules.doc:
This module provides a home for electrical and thermal transport, linear and thermoelectric
response, optical response, and nonlinear response.

modules.title: Thermoelectric figure of merit
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

A thermoelectric material converts a temperature difference into electrical
power. In the linear-response (Onsager) regime, the coupled transport of
charge and heat in an isotropic material is governed by the constitutive
relations

  J = σ (E − S ∇T),        q = T S J − κ ∇T,

so a thermoelectric material is characterized by exactly four transport
coefficients: the Seebeck coefficient `S`, the electrical conductivity `σ`,
and the thermal conductivity `κ = κl + κe`, split into its lattice (phonon)
and electronic contributions because the two channels respond independently
to material design. These four coefficients are collected in the structure
`ThermoelectricMaterial`, and everything in this file is stated on it.

The performance of the material at absolute temperature `T` is captured by
the dimensionless figure of merit

  zT = σ S² T / (κl + κe),

whose numerator groups into the power factor `PF = σ S²`. Temperature is a
state variable, not a material property, so `T` enters as an argument rather
than a field. The four coefficients of a real material are themselves
temperature-dependent, so a `ThermoelectricMaterial` should be read as a
material at an operating point, its coefficients evaluated at the same
temperature at which `zT` is evaluated.

In this file all quantities are real numbers in a fixed consistent system of
units, following the convention of `Physlib.Thermodynamics.IdealGas.Basic`.

## ii. Key results

- `ThermoelectricMaterial`: the four linear-response transport coefficients
  of a thermoelectric material, with their physical sign constraints.
- `powerFactor`: the thermoelectric power factor `σ S²`.
- `totalThermalConductivity`: the total thermal conductivity `κl + κe`.
- `figureOfMerit`: the dimensionless figure of merit `zT`.
- `figureOfMerit_eq`: the flat form `zT = σ S² T / (κl + κe)`.
- `figureOfMerit_pos`: positivity of `zT` for a material with a nonzero
  Seebeck coefficient at positive temperature.
- `figureOfMerit_le_of_le`: lowering the lattice thermal conductivity raises
  `zT`, the phonon-glass electron-crystal design principle.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The thermoelectric material
- B. The power factor
- C. The total thermal conductivity
- D. The figure of merit
  - D.1. Equalities for the figure of merit
  - D.2. Positivity of the figure of merit
  - D.3. Monotonicity in the lattice thermal conductivity

## iv. References

* Ioffe, A.F., Semiconductor Thermoelements and Thermoelectric Cooling, Infosearch (1957).
  [ref: ioffe_1957]
* Snyder, G.J., Toberer, E.S., Complex thermoelectric materials, Nature Materials 7, 105–114
  (2008). [ref: snyder_toberer_2008]

sections.text:
## A. The thermoelectric material

The four fields are the complete set of linear-response coefficients for
coupled charge and heat transport in an isotropic material: no further
material parameter enters the steady-state thermoelectric equations, and
`zT` is a function of exactly these four together with the temperature.
The sign constraints are physical: a thermoelectric material conducts
charge (`0 < σ`) and its lattice conducts heat (`0 < κl`), while the
electronic heat channel can be negligible but never negative (`0 ≤ κe`).
The Seebeck coefficient is unconstrained: its sign records the carrier
type (negative for electrons, positive for holes), and it vanishes at
compensation points.
## B. The power factor
## C. The total thermal conductivity
## D. The figure of merit
### D.1. Equalities for the figure of merit
### D.2. Positivity of the figure of merit
### D.3. Monotonicity in the lattice thermal conductivity

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial
declarations.doc:
A thermoelectric material in the linear-response regime, characterized by
its four transport coefficients.
declarations.statement:
structure ThermoelectricMaterial where
  /-- The Seebeck coefficient `S`: the voltage developed per unit temperature
  difference. Its sign records the dominant carrier type. -/
  S : ℝ
  /-- The electrical conductivity `σ`. -/
  σ : ℝ
  /-- The lattice (phonon) contribution `κl` to the thermal conductivity. -/
  κl : ℝ
  /-- The electronic contribution `κe` to the thermal conductivity. -/
  κe : ℝ
  σ_pos : 0 < σ
  κl_pos : 0 < κl
  κe_nonneg : 0 ≤ κe

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.powerFactor
declarations.doc: The thermoelectric power factor `PF = σ S²` of a material.
declarations.statement: def powerFactor (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.powerFactor_pos
declarations.doc: The power factor is positive when the Seebeck coefficient is nonzero.
declarations.statement:
lemma powerFactor_pos {M : ThermoelectricMaterial} (hS : M.S ≠ 0) :
    0 < M.powerFactor

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.totalThermalConductivity
declarations.doc:
The total thermal conductivity `κl + κe` of a material, the sum of the
lattice (phonon) and electronic contributions.
declarations.statement: def totalThermalConductivity (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.totalThermalConductivity_pos
declarations.doc: The total thermal conductivity is positive.
declarations.statement:
lemma totalThermalConductivity_pos (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) :
    0 < M.totalThermalConductivity

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit
declarations.doc:
The dimensionless thermoelectric figure of merit
`zT = PF · T / (κl + κe)` of a material at absolute temperature `T`.
declarations.statement: def figureOfMerit (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) (T : ℝ) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_eq
declarations.doc:
The figure of merit in its standard flat form
`zT = σ S² T / (κl + κe)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma figureOfMerit_eq (M : ThermoelectricMaterial) (T : ℝ) :
    M.figureOfMerit T = M.σ * M.S ^ 2 * T / (M.κl + M.κe)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_pos
declarations.doc:
The figure of merit is positive at positive temperature when the Seebeck
coefficient is nonzero.

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.ThermoelectricMaterial.figureOfMerit_le_of_le
declarations.doc:
Lowering the lattice thermal conductivity raises the figure of merit: if
`M.κl ≤ κl'` then the material with lattice conductivity `κl'` (all other
coefficients equal) has the smaller `zT`. This is the phonon-glass
electron-crystal design principle: scatter phonons without degrading
electronic transport. Note the hypotheses: no condition on the Seebeck
coefficient is needed, since monotonicity only requires the numerator
`σ S² T` to be nonnegative.

modules.title: The tight binding chain
modules.doc:
## i. Overview

The tight binding chain corresponds to an electron in motion
in a 1d solid with the assumption the electron can sit only on the atoms of the solid.

The solid is assumed to consist of `N` sites with a separation of `a` between them

Mathematically, the tight binding chain corresponds to a
QM problem located on a lattice with only self and nearest neighbour interactions,
with periodic boundary conditions.

## ii. Key results

- `TightBindingChain` : The physical parameters making up the tight binding chain.
- `localizedState` : The orthonormal basis of localized states.
- `hamiltonian` : The Hamiltonian of the tight binding chain.
- `BrillouinZone` : The Brillouin zone of the tight binding chain.
- `QuantaWaveNumber` : The quantized wavenumbers of the energy eigenstates.
- `energyEigenstate` : The energy eigenstates of the tight binding chain.
- `energyEigenbasis` : The orthonormal basis of normalized energy eigenstates.
- `energyEigenvalue` : The energy eigenvalues of the tight binding chain.
- `hamiltonian_energyEigenstate` : The Hamiltonian acting on an energy eigenstate
  gives the corresponding energy eigenvalue times the energy eigenstate.
- `hasEigenvalue_hamiltonian_iff` : The eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian are exactly the
  energy eigenvalues.

## iii. Table of contents

- A. The setup
  - A.1. The input data for the tight binding chain
  - A.2. The Hilbert space
- B. The localized states
  - B.1. The orthonormal basis of localized states
  - B.2. Notation for localized states
  - B.3. Orthonormality of the localized states
- C. The operator `|m⟩⟨n|`
  - C.1. Definition of the operator `|m⟩⟨n|`
  - C.2. Notation for the operator `|m⟩⟨n|`
  - C.3. The operator `|m⟩⟨n|` applied to a localized state
- D. The Hamiltonian of the tight binding chain
  - D.1. Hermiticity of the Hamiltonian
  - D.2. Hamiltonian applied to a localized state
  - D.3. Mean energy of a localized state
- E. The Brillouin zone and quantized wavenumbers
  - E.1. The Brillouin zone
  - E.2. The quantized wavenumbers of the energy eigenstates
  - E.3. Wavenumbers lie in the Brillouin zone
  - E.4. Expotentials related to the quantized wavenumbers
- F. The energy eigenstates and eigenvalues
  - F.1. The energy eigenstates
  - F.2. Orthonormality of the energy eigenstates
  - F.3. The energy eigenvalues
  - F.4. The time-independent Schrodinger equation
  - F.5. The spectrum of the Hamiltonian

## iv. References

* https://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/user/tong/aqm/aqmtwo.pdf. [ref: tong_statistical_physics]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain
declarations.doc: The physical parameters making up the tight binding chain.
declarations.statement:
structure TightBindingChain where
  /-- The number of sites, or atoms, in the chain -/
  N : Nat
  [N_ne_zero : NeZero N]
  /-- The distance between the sites -/
  a : ℝ
  a_pos : 0 < a
  /-- The energy associate with a particle sitting at a fixed site. -/
  E0 : ℝ
  /-- The hopping parameter. -/
  t : ℝ
instance : NeZero T.N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.HilbertSpace
declarations.doc:
The Hilbert space of a `TightBindingchain` is the `N`-dimensional finite dimensional
Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: abbrev HilbertSpace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.finrank_hilbertSpace
declarations.doc: The Hilbert space of the chain has dimension `N`.
declarations.statement: lemma finrank_hilbertSpace : Module.finrank ℂ T.HilbertSpace = T.N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedState
declarations.doc: The eigenstate corresponding to the particle been located on the `n`th site.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedState {T : TightBindingChain} :
    OrthonormalBasis (Fin T.N) ℂ (HilbertSpace T)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedState_orthonormal
declarations.doc: The localized states are normalized.
declarations.statement: lemma localizedState_orthonormal : Orthonormal ℂ (localizedState (T := T))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedState_orthonormal_eq_ite
declarations.statement:
lemma localizedState_orthonormal_eq_ite (m n : Fin T.N) :
    ⟨m|n⟩ = if m = n then 1 else 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedComp
declarations.doc: The linear map `|m⟩⟨n|` for `⟨n|` localized states.
declarations.statement:
noncomputable def localizedComp {T : TightBindingChain} (m n : Fin T.N) :
    T.HilbertSpace →ₗ[ℂ] T.HilbertSpace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedComp_apply_localizedState
declarations.statement: lemma localizedComp_apply_localizedState (m n p : Fin T.N) :

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.localizedComp_adjoint
declarations.doc: The adjoint of localizedComp |m⟩⟨n| is |n⟩⟨m|.
declarations.statement:
lemma localizedComp_adjoint (m n : Fin T.N) (ψ φ : T.HilbertSpace) :
    ⟪|m⟩⟨n| ψ, φ⟫_ℂ = ⟪ψ, |n⟩⟨m| φ⟫_ℂ := by
  simp only [localizedComp, LinearMap.coe_mk, AddHom.coe_mk, inner_smul_left, inner_smul_right,
    inner_conj_symm]
  ring

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hamiltonian
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian of the tight binding chain with periodic
boundary conditions is given by `E₀ ∑ n, |n⟩⟨n| - t ∑ n, (|n⟩⟨n + 1| + |n + 1⟩⟨n|)`.
The periodic boundary conditions is manifested by the `+` in `n + 1` being
within `Fin T.N` (that is modulo `T.N`).
declarations.statement: noncomputable def hamiltonian : T.HilbertSpace →ₗ[ℂ] T.HilbertSpace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hamiltonian_hermitian
declarations.doc: The hamiltonian of the tight binding chain is hermitian.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_hermitian (ψ φ : T.HilbertSpace) :
    ⟪T.hamiltonian ψ, φ⟫_ℂ = ⟪ψ, T.hamiltonian φ⟫_ℂ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hamiltonian_apply_localizedState
declarations.doc:
The Hamiltonian applied to the localized state `|n⟩` gives
`T.E0 • |n⟩ - T.t • (|n + 1⟩ + |n - 1⟩)`.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_apply_localizedState (n : Fin T.N) :
    T.hamiltonian |n⟩ = (T.E0 : ℂ) • |n⟩ - (T.t : ℂ) • (|n + 1⟩ + |n - 1⟩) := by
  simp only [hamiltonian, LinearMap.sub_apply, LinearMap.smul_apply, LinearMap.coe_sum,
    Finset.sum_apply, LinearMap.add_apply, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib,
    localizedComp_apply_localizedState, ← eq_sub_iff_add_eq, Finset.sum_ite_eq', Finset.mem_univ,
    ite_true]
  module

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energy_localizedState
declarations.doc:
The energy of a localized state in the tight binding chain is `E0`.
This lemma assumes that there is more then one site in the chain otherwise the
result is not true.
declarations.statement:
lemma energy_localizedState (n : Fin T.N) (htn : 1 < T.N) : ⟪|n⟩, T.hamiltonian |n⟩⟫_ℂ = T.E0 := by
  rw [hamiltonian_apply_localizedState]
  simp only [smul_add, inner_sub_right, inner_add_right, inner_smul_right,
    localizedState_orthonormal_eq_ite, ↓reduceIte, mul_one, left_eq_add, eq_sub_iff_add_eq,
    add_eq_left, Fin.one_eq_zero_iff, mul_ite, mul_zero, sub_eq_self]
  simp [show T.N ≠ 1 from by omega]

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.BrillouinZone
declarations.doc:
The Brillouin zone of the tight binding model is `[-π/a, π/a)`.
This is the set in which wave functions are uniquely defined.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def BrillouinZone : Set ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.QuantaWaveNumber
declarations.doc:
The wavenumbers associated with the energy eigenstates.
This corresponds to the set `2 π / (a N) * (n - ⌊N/2⌋)` for `n : Fin T.N`.
It is defined as such so it sits in the Brillouin zone.
declarations.statement: def QuantaWaveNumber : Set ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber
declarations.doc: The quantized wavenumber `2 π / (a N) * (n - ⌊N/2⌋)` of the index `n`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def quantaWaveNumber (n : Fin T.N) : T.QuantaWaveNumber

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_injective
declarations.doc: Distinct indices give distinct quantized wavenumbers.
declarations.statement: lemma quantaWaveNumber_injective : Function.Injective T.quantaWaveNumber

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_subset_brillouinZone
declarations.doc: The quantized wavenumbers form a subset of the `BrillouinZone`.
declarations.statement: lemma quantaWaveNumber_subset_brillouinZone : T.QuantaWaveNumber ⊆ T.BrillouinZone

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_exp_N
declarations.statement:
lemma quantaWaveNumber_exp_N (n : ℕ) (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * n * T.N * T.a) = 1

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_exp_sub_one
declarations.statement:
lemma quantaWaveNumber_exp_sub_one (n : Fin T.N) (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * (n - 1).val * T.a) =
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * n * T.a) * Complex.exp (- Complex.I * k * T.a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.quantaWaveNumber_exp_add_one
declarations.statement:
lemma quantaWaveNumber_exp_add_one (n : Fin T.N) (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * (n + 1).val * T.a) =
    Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * n * T.a) * Complex.exp (Complex.I * k * T.a)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate
declarations.doc:
The energy eigenstates of the tight binding chain They are given by
`∑ n, exp (I * k * n * T.a) • |n⟩`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def energyEigenstate (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) : T.HilbertSpace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_ne_zero
declarations.doc: An energy eigenstate is not zero.
declarations.statement: lemma energyEigenstate_ne_zero (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) : T.energyEigenstate k ≠ 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_inner_self
declarations.doc: The inner product of an energy eigenstate with itself is `N`.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenstate_inner_self (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    ⟪T.energyEigenstate k, T.energyEigenstate k⟫_ℂ = T.N

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_orthogonal
declarations.doc:
The energy eigenstates of the tight binding chain are orthogonal.

This is a fundamental quantum mechanical result: eigenstates of a Hermitian operator
(the Hamiltonian) with distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal. Here we prove it directly
using the periodic boundary conditions which quantize the wavenumbers.

The key physical insight is that different wavenumbers k₁ ≠ k₂ give rise to different
N-th roots of unity exp(i(k₂-k₁)a), and the sum of all N-th roots of unity equals zero.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenstate_orthogonal :
    Pairwise fun k1 k2 => ⟪T.energyEigenstate k1, T.energyEigenstate k2⟫_ℂ = 0

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_linearIndependent
declarations.doc: The energy eigenstates are linearly independent.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenstate_linearIndependent :
    LinearIndependent ℂ (fun n : Fin T.N => T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_span
declarations.doc: The energy eigenstates span the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenstate_span :
    ⊤ ≤ Submodule.span ℂ (Set.range fun n : Fin T.N =>
      T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenstate_orthonormal
declarations.doc: The normalized energy eigenstates `N ^ (-1/2) • energyEigenstate k` are orthonormal.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenstate_orthonormal :
    Orthonormal ℂ (fun n : Fin T.N =>
      (((Real.sqrt T.N)⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n))

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenbasis
declarations.doc: The normalized energy eigenstates form an orthonormal basis of the Hilbert space.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def energyEigenbasis : OrthonormalBasis (Fin T.N) ℂ T.HilbertSpace

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenbasis_apply
declarations.doc:
The `n`-th vector of the basis is the normalized energy eigenstate of the `n`-th
wavenumber.
declarations.statement:
lemma energyEigenbasis_apply (n : Fin T.N) :
    T.energyEigenbasis n =
      (((Real.sqrt T.N)⁻¹ : ℝ) : ℂ) • T.energyEigenstate (T.quantaWaveNumber n)

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.energyEigenvalue
declarations.doc:
The energy eigenvalue of the tight binding chain for a `k` in `QuantaWaveNumber` is
`E0 - 2 * t * Real.cos (k * T.a)`.
declarations.statement: noncomputable def energyEigenvalue (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) : ℝ

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hamiltonian_energyEigenstate
declarations.doc: The energy eigenstates satisfy the time-independent Schrodinger equation.
declarations.statement:
lemma hamiltonian_energyEigenstate (k : T.QuantaWaveNumber) :
    T.hamiltonian (T.energyEigenstate k) = T.energyEigenvalue k• T.energyEigenstate k

declarations.name: CondensedMatter.TightBindingChain.hasEigenvalue_hamiltonian_iff
declarations.doc:
The eigenvalues of the Hamiltonian are exactly the energies `E0 - 2 t cos (k a)` of the
quantized wavenumbers.
declarations.statement:
lemma hasEigenvalue_hamiltonian_iff (E : ℂ) :
    Module.End.HasEigenvalue T.hamiltonian E ↔
      ∃ k : T.QuantaWaveNumber, E = T.energyEigenvalue k

modules.title: A. Topological condensed matter
modules.doc:
This module provides a home for topological invariants of bands, Chern and topological
insulators, Weyl and nodal semimetals, topological superconductors, symmetry-protected phases,
and interacting topological phases. It distinguishes local band geometry from global
topological invariants.
